messages:
mia: Heads-up: saw a metrics mismatch on the rollout page this morning. Quick repro below.

alex: details?

mia: Steps: 1) open console, 2) switch to org A, 3) open Rollouts -> Traffic, 4) quickly switch to org B, 5) refresh. The traffic graph still shows org A's lanes for a few seconds and quota counters spike for the wrong org.

sam: ugh. I just hit this too — noticed it when doing a canary swap. UI showed 5% traffic for a service in org A while I was in org B.

devon: can you paste any logs or headers from the frontend/gateway?

mia: captured a console dump: 
```
GET /api/internal/rollouts/traffic?org_id=org-b 200 OK 
request headers: {"x-org-id": "org-b", "x-route-affinity": "rollout-V3"}
response payload: {"lanes": [{"org_id": "org-a", "percent": 5}, ...]}
localStorage: {"lastOrg": "org-b", "rolloutCache_v2": "eyJvcmdfaWQiOiJvcmdhIn0="}
```

kia: sounds like the internal API returned the wrong payload despite the header being org-b. Is the gateway stripping or reusing cache entries?

alex: quick theory: the internal proxy layer uses a shared cache keyed by route only, not by org header. So when requests come in quick succession with different x-org-id, we can serve stale cached responses.

sam: that matches. I saw a related bug where quota-keys were only route+model, not org-scoped. Might be the same cache key smell.

devon: Is this primarily a client-side cache issue or backend cache? The snippet shows response payload with org_a so backend returned it.

alex: backend returned wrong object because cache miss logic wrong. The data service populates Redis with cache key = rollout:traffic:rollout-V3. No org suffix.

mia: possible quick mitigation: have the frontend append ?org_id to the cache key or include org in the cache-control header to force bypass. But that's a bandaid.

sam: I think short-term we should: 1) patch gateway to include org in cache key (low-risk), 2) clear stale cache entries for rollout routes, 3) add a client-side guard to discard responses where payload.org_id != currentOrg (defensive).

kia: agree on layered approach. Gateway patch is owner-bounded to alex. Client guard is a tiny PR for console (owner sam). Ops can run a script to evict keys.

devon: logging/telemetry gap: because telemetry events are attributed to org A (wrong), our cost metrics will be skewed. We need to backfill/annotate events or at least flag the window.

ops-bot: incident-notice: created incident INC-2026, severity: low-medium, implicated services: gateway, rollout-service, console.

alex: I'll own the gateway fix. Plan: add org id to Redis cache key and make it configurable via feature flag. Will put up PR today, request review from kia. Will also add telemetry metric for cache hits labeled by org header to detect regressions.

sam: I'll put up the console guard change + small e2e asserting payload.org_id === currentOrg. Also add a warning banner when mismatch detected to avoid accidental admin actions.

mia: can we also add an automated test that simulates rapid org switch and ensures the UI doesn't show mixed lanes?

kia: yes. I'll add a test in rollout-service integration suite to hit the cache with alternating headers and assert responses are org-specific.

devon: for immediate cleanup, ops: can you run: 
```
redis-cli KEYS "rollout:traffic:*" | xargs -n1 redis-cli DEL
```

ops-bot: ops-queue: tag @ops on INC-2026 for cache eviction.

sam: who will canary the gateway change? alex: can we target dedicated staging first, then a 10% canary in prod with metric alerts?

alex: yep. Staging -> canary 10% -> 50% -> prod. Add alert: cache-hit-rate by org dips below 95% or any src header mismatch >0.1% within 5m.

mia: timeline?

alex: aim to merge by EOD, deploy to staging tonight. sam, can you do the console PR early tomorrow?

sam: yes, I have a tiny patch ready. Will tag @devon for telemetry adjustments.

devon: I'll add a one-off job to scan telemetry events between 02:00-03:00 UTC for possible misattribution windows and annotate them with method=cache-key-mismatch.

kia: also note: this pattern might exist for other route-cached endpoints (quota, prefetch). We should run a service-wide grep for cache keys missing org or workspace scope. I'll run that and post results.

mia: thanks all. Leaving a note: workaround for admins — refresh the page or open in incognito after switching orgs until patch lands.

alex: assigning: alex (gateway), sam (console guard), kia (integration tests/grep), devon (telemetry backfill), ops (cache eviction).

ops-bot: INC-2026 updated: owners assigned.

sam: quick follow-up: I added a short snippet to console to drop responses if mismatch and log an error: 
```
if (payload.org_id !== currentOrg) {
  console.warn('org mismatch, discarding response', payload.org_id, currentOrg);
  return;
}
```

alex: that's fine for now. We'll remove after stable canary.

kia: posted initial grep results: found 4 services using route-only cache keys: rollout-service, quota-service, prefetch-proxy, insights-aggregator. Will open issues.

mia: perfect. Let's keep the thread updated as canary progresses. :eyes:
